h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תָבוֹא, י׳ Ki Savo, 10
Consolation Restores the Covenant Through Teshuvah and Enduring Holiness

p: It is brought in Likkutei Torah
from the Arizal, of blessed memory,
are a rectification for the blemish of the covenant;
And one may say that to allude to this,
of the number of the seven of consolation,
to the aspect of the holiness of Yesod,
"the tzaddik is the foundation of the world" (Mishlei 10:25).
קוּמִי אוֹרִי כִּי בָא אוֹרֵךְ וְגוֹמֵר (יְשַׁעְיָה ס, א)
"Arise, shine, for your light has come, etc." (Yeshayahu 60:1).
And as is known, the aspect of light
alludes to the holiness of the covenant,
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Taanis 15a):
and the tzaddik is the one who guards the covenant,
And for this the promise comes
that a person's heart should not fall within him:
even if it happened to him
that he blemished in this matter,
let him not say in his heart, "It is hopeless,"
if only he will set his heart
from now on to improve his ways,
which is a matter of arousal
to this holiness from the side of man;
about Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him:
and the glory of Hashem has shone upon you"
that Hashem, may He be blessed, will complete it for him
to shine this holiness upon him,
so that he will come to the ultimate rectification.
"For behold, darkness shall cover the earth,
וְעָלַיִךְ יִזְרַח ה׳ וְגוֹמֵר (שָׁם ס, ב)
but upon you Hashem will shine, etc." (ibid. 60:2).
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת זֶהוּ כָּל עִנְיַן וְהָעֵסֶק
For in truth this is the whole matter and purpose
of the rebukes and the suffering of the exiles:
so that the opposite be destroyed,
And all the curses stated in the rebuke
in the language of a curse,
but within them is set every good,
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (זֹהַר חָדָשׁ תָּבוֹא)
as is brought in the Zohar Chadash on this parshah (Zohar Chadash, Ki Savo).
And this is what is said,
"And they shall be upon you for a sign and for a wonder,
And according to its plain meaning,
שֶׁהוּא מוּסָב לְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר לְמַעְלָה מִזֶּה
that it refers to what is said above it,
וּבָאוּ עָלֶיךָ כָּל הַקְּלָלוֹת הָאֵלֶּה וְגוֹמֵר
"And all these curses shall come upon you, etc.,
is it conceivable, according to its plain meaning,
that it should be so, Heaven forbid, forever?
Are not all the verses of the Torah full of this,
that we will merit in the future
לִהְיוֹת עֶלְיוֹן עַל כָּל גּוֹיֵי הָאָרֶץ
to be supreme over all the nations of the earth,
and all kinds of promises and good things
"And they shall be upon you for a sign and for a wonder,"
כִּי אוֹת הִיא בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵיכֶם וְגוֹמֵר (שְׁמוֹת לא, יג)
"For it is a sign between Me and you, etc." (Shemos 31:13),
"And as for Me, this is My covenant with them, etc.:
they shall not depart from your mouth, etc.,
will be a sign and a wonder:
are only temporary, on the surface,
but in truth the holiness of Yisrael
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה ט, א)
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sotah 9a):
but they will not be spent."
וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּהַתּוֹכָחָה
And this is also what is said in the rebuke,
"and you shall have no assurance of your life" (Devarim 28:66):
that he will not believe in himself
that he has the vitality of holiness;
in all the souls of Yisrael,
and it will never be interrupted,
וְזֶה יֵשׁ לְרַמֵּז גַּם כֵּן בַּפָּסוּק
And this can also be alluded to in the pasuk,
"When Hashem returns the captivity of Tziyon,
that is, in the future we will see palpably
as is brought in the Gemara (Berachos 55a):
For this is the matter of the rebukes:
that they were said only to frighten
so that he will improve his way from now on,
and automatically they will all be turned to good.
and he interpreted the very verses for good;
the verses themselves will be turned to good.
And the end of the haftarah is,
they shall inherit the land forever" (Yeshayahu 60:21):
will be called by the name "righteous,"
even if something passed over them,
because "forever they shall inherit the land,"
which is the attribute of Yaakov,
is found in all the souls of Yisrael,
שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד (מִשְׁלֵי יב, יט)
"The lip of truth shall be established forever" (Mishlei 12:19).
And therefore, even if at times
he blemished the aspect of tzaddik,
he can return to his holiness
And about this it says, "the shoot of My planting" (ibid.),
"And I planted you a noble vine,
"The work of My hands, in which to glory":
שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁעָבַר עָלָיו עַד כֹּה
that all that passed over him until now
was the work of the hands of Hashem, may He be blessed,
so that from it would come
the aspect of the glory of Yisrael,
when he will be rectified for the good.

p: And one may allude to this matter
in the episode of Rabbi Elazar the son of Rabbi Shimon,
who was strolling on the riverbank,
that he had learned much Torah
that is, he then saw in his soul
how he was guarded and pure
in the holiness of the covenant, greatly.
There chanced upon him a certain man
of the blemish of the covenant;
for he is the opposite of the guardian of the covenant,
as it says regarding Yosef HaTzaddik,
"Go and say to the Craftsman who made me, etc."
may he be remembered for good.
is the angel of the covenant,
Rabbi Elazar the son of Rabbi Shimon
לְהוֹכִיחוֹ עַל מַה שֶּׁגִּינָּה כָּל כָּךְ
to rebuke him for disparaging so much
as if, Heaven forbid, his hope were lost.
but if only he will set his heart
to improve his way from now on,
all that has already come upon him,
"Go to the Craftsman who made me."
that all that passed over him
הָיָה גַּם כֵּן מֵרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
was also from the will of Hashem, may He be blessed,
שֶׁבָּרָא אֶת הָאָדָם עִם הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע
Who created man with the yetzer hara,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֻכָּה נב, ב)
and as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sukkah 52b):
and were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him,
he could not prevail over it."
It emerges that this person can come
that, as it were, Hashem, may He be blessed,
was the cause and the Craftsman,
because He then withdrew the help from him
in Kayin's claim to Hashem, may He be blessed:
when He asked him, "Where is Hevel your brother?"
and as is brought in the Midrash (Tanchuma Bereishis 9):
הֲלֹא אַתָּה בָּרָאתָ בִּי הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע
Did You not create in me the evil inclination,
was a claim that was heard,
since this is written in the holy Torah;
since Hashem, may He be blessed, spoke and argued with him,
certainly his soul was very lofty,
for he was the first offspring
מִיצִיר כַּפָּיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
of the handiwork of the Holy One, blessed be He.
And as is brought in the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 22:13),
and Heaven forbid that the strap be loosened
to do whatever his heart desires.
Only the person who knows in his soul
all the lofty levels that he attains,
are only from Hashem, may He be blessed,
and not at all from his own strength and effort
when a stumbling block, Heaven forbid, comes before him,
he can strengthen himself in his heart
that this too is from Hashem, may He be blessed.
And this may be the intent
בְּמַה שֶּׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
of what David HaMelech, peace be upon him, said:
"If I ascend to heaven, You are there;
and if I make my bed in the grave, behold, You are there" (Tehillim 139:8).
That is, if at the time that a person goes
שֶׁהוּא רַק מִכֹּחַ וּמֵעֵזֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
that it is only by the power and help of Hashem, may He be blessed
אָז אֲפִילּוּ כְּשֶׁיִּזְדַּמֵּן לוֹ לִפְעָמִים נְפִילָה
then even when at times a fall comes his way,
which is "if I make my bed in the grave,"
and he can strengthen himself with this
so as not to fall in his own eyes,
and by this power he will strengthen himself to return.
"Even when I walk in the valley of the shadow of death,
and the least a mighty nation;
אֲנִי ה׳ בְּעִתָּהּ אֲחִישֶׁנָּה (יְשַׁעְיָה ס, כב)
I, Hashem, will hasten it in its time" (Yeshayahu 60:22).
